dishes.name: Risotto alla Milanese
dishes.desc: Creamy risotto cooked with beef stock, butter, Parmesan and saffron, giving it a golden colour; classic of Milan.

dishes.name: Ossobuco
dishes.desc: Cross-cut veal shanks braised slowly with white wine, vegetables and broth, traditionally served with gremolata and saffron risotto.

dishes.name: Polenta
dishes.desc: Thick porridge of boiled cornmeal, served soft or set and grilled, alongside stews, cheese or mushrooms.

dishes.name: Tagliatelle al Ragù
dishes.desc: Flat egg ribbon pasta tossed with Bologna's slow-cooked meat sauce of beef, pork, soffritto, wine and a little tomato.

dishes.name: Tortellini in Brodo
dishes.desc: Small ring-shaped pasta filled with pork, prosciutto and Parmesan, served in rich capon or beef broth, a Christmas tradition in Emilia.

dishes.name: Lasagne alla Bolognese
dishes.desc: Baked layers of green egg pasta sheets, meat ragù, béchamel and Parmigiano-Reggiano from Emilia-Romagna.

dishes.name: Pesto alla Genovese
dishes.desc: Ligurian raw sauce of pounded basil, pine nuts, garlic, Parmesan, pecorino and olive oil, tossed with trofie or trenette.

dishes.name: Focaccia Genovese
dishes.desc: Flat, dimpled Ligurian bread generously soaked with olive oil and brine and sprinkled with coarse salt.

dishes.name: Bagna Cauda
dishes.desc: Piedmontese warm dip of garlic, anchovies and olive oil, kept hot at the table for dipping raw and cooked vegetables.

dishes.name: Vitello Tonnato
dishes.desc: Chilled thin slices of poached veal covered with a creamy sauce of tuna, capers, anchovies and mayonnaise; Piedmontese summer dish.

dishes.name: Cotoletta alla Milanese
dishes.desc: Bone-in veal chop coated in egg and breadcrumbs and fried in clarified butter, a Milanese classic.

dishes.name: Pizzoccheri
dishes.desc: Short buckwheat tagliatelle from Valtellina baked with potatoes, savoy cabbage, Casera cheese, garlic and butter.

dishes.name: Panettone
dishes.desc: Tall, domed Milanese sweet bread with candied citrus and raisins, eaten at Christmas and New Year.

dishes.name: Tiramisu
dishes.desc: Layered dessert of coffee-soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream dusted with cocoa, from the Veneto.

dishes.name: Minestrone
dishes.desc: Thick vegetable soup with beans, seasonal vegetables and often pasta or rice, made across Italy.

dishes.name: Panna Cotta
dishes.desc: Piedmontese dessert of sweetened cream set with gelatine, served with berry sauce or caramel.

dishes.name: Prosciutto di Parma
dishes.desc: Dry-cured ham from Parma aged for at least a year, sliced paper-thin and eaten with melon or bread.

dishes.name: Spritz
dishes.desc: Venetian aperitivo of prosecco, a bitter orange liqueur and soda water, served over ice with an orange slice.

dishes.name: Piadina
dishes.desc: Romagna flatbread of flour, lard and salt, folded around prosciutto, soft squacquerone cheese and rocket.

dishes.name: Carpaccio
dishes.desc: Paper-thin raw beef drizzled with a light mustard mayonnaise, created at Harry's Bar in Venice.

dishes.name: Canederli
dishes.desc: South Tyrolean bread dumplings with speck, served in clear broth or with melted butter.

dishes.name: Parmigiano-Reggiano
dishes.desc: Hard cow's milk cheese from Parma and Reggio Emilia aged for at least a year, broken into crumbly chunks or grated over pasta.

dishes.name: Gorgonzola
dishes.desc: Blue-veined cow's milk cheese from Lombardy and Piedmont, sweet and creamy (dolce) or firm and sharp (piccante).

dishes.name: Bresaola
dishes.desc: Lean beef salted and air-dried in the Valtellina, sliced paper-thin and dressed with olive oil, lemon and rocket.

dishes.name: Speck Alto Adige
dishes.desc: South Tyrolean ham, lightly smoked over beech wood and air-dried with juniper and herbs.

dishes.name: Mortadella
dishes.desc: Large Bolognese pork sausage studded with cubes of fat and pistachios, sliced thin for sandwiches.

dishes.name: Prosecco
dishes.desc: Light sparkling white wine of glera grapes from the hills of the Veneto and Friuli.

dishes.name: Bollito Misto
dishes.desc: Piedmontese platter of boiled beef, veal, tongue, hen and cotechino with salsa verde and mostarda.

dishes.name: Agnolotti del Plin
dishes.desc: Tiny pinched Piedmontese pasta parcels filled with roast meats, served with butter and sage or roast juices.

dishes.name: Grissini
dishes.desc: Thin crisp breadsticks from Turin, hand-stretched to the length of an arm.

dishes.name: Pandoro
dishes.desc: Tall star-shaped Christmas sweet bread from Verona, dusted with vanilla icing sugar.

dishes.name: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
dishes.desc: Roman pasta tossed with guanciale, egg yolks, pecorino romano and black pepper, without cream.

dishes.name: Cacio e Pepe
dishes.desc: Roman pasta, usually tonnarelli or spaghetti, coated in a creamy emulsion of pecorino romano, black pepper and pasta water.

dishes.name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
dishes.desc: Thick hollow spaghetti in a sauce of guanciale, tomato, pecorino and chilli, named after the town of Amatrice.

dishes.name: Saltimbocca alla Romana
dishes.desc: Thin veal escalopes topped with prosciutto and sage, pan-fried and finished with white wine and butter.

dishes.name: Supplì
dishes.desc: Roman fried rice croquettes filled with tomato-sauced rice and a melting core of mozzarella.

dishes.name: Carciofi alla Giudia
dishes.desc: Whole artichokes flattened and deep-fried twice until crisp, a speciality of Rome's Jewish quarter.

dishes.name: Porchetta
dishes.desc: Boneless whole pig rolled with garlic, fennel, rosemary and pepper and slow-roasted, often sold sliced in bread rolls; famous from Ariccia.

dishes.name: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
dishes.desc: Thick T-bone steak of Chianina beef grilled over embers, served rare with olive oil and salt in Florence.

dishes.name: Ribollita
dishes.desc: Tuscan reboiled soup of cannellini beans, cavolo nero, vegetables and stale bread.

dishes.name: Pappa al Pomodoro
dishes.desc: Thick Tuscan soup of ripe tomatoes, stale bread, garlic, basil and olive oil, served warm or cold.

dishes.name: Panzanella
dishes.desc: Tuscan summer salad of soaked stale bread, tomatoes, onions, basil, olive oil and vinegar.

dishes.name: Pecorino Romano
dishes.desc: Hard, salty sheep's milk cheese from Lazio and Sardinia, grated over Roman pastas or eaten in chunks.

dishes.name: Coda alla Vaccinara
dishes.desc: Roman oxtail stew braised for hours with tomato, celery, wine and sometimes cocoa, raisins and pine nuts.

dishes.name: Bruschetta
dishes.desc: Grilled bread rubbed with garlic and drizzled with olive oil, often topped with chopped tomatoes and basil.

dishes.name: Gnocchi alla Romana
dishes.desc: Rounds of semolina cooked in milk, layered with butter and Parmesan and baked until golden.

dishes.name: Arrosticini
dishes.desc: Abruzzo skewers of small mutton cubes grilled over a long narrow brazier and eaten by the dozen.

dishes.name: Pallotte Cacio e Uova
dishes.desc: Abruzzese balls of pecorino, egg and breadcrumbs, fried and then simmered in tomato sauce.

dishes.name: Negroni
dishes.desc: Florentine cocktail of equal parts gin, red vermouth and red bitter, stirred over ice with orange peel.

dishes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
dishes.desc: Thick soup of short pasta and borlotti beans with tomato, garlic and rosemary, Italian home cooking.

dishes.name: Cantucci
dishes.desc: Twice-baked Tuscan almond biscuits, dipped in Vin Santo after dinner.

dishes.name: Olive Ascolane
dishes.desc: Large green olives stuffed with minced meat, breaded and deep-fried, from Ascoli Piceno.

dishes.name: Lampredotto
dishes.desc: Florentine sandwich of slow-simmered cow's stomach topped with green sauce, the roll dipped in the broth.

dishes.name: Pizza Napoletana
dishes.desc: Soft, thin-centred pizza with a puffy, charred crust, baked for about a minute in a wood-fired oven in Naples.

dishes.name: Pizza Margherita
dishes.desc: Neapolitan pizza topped with tomato, mozzarella, fresh basil and olive oil in the colours of the Italian flag.

dishes.name: Spaghetti alle Vongole
dishes.desc: Spaghetti with clams cooked in olive oil, garlic, white wine, chilli and parsley, a Neapolitan classic.

dishes.name: Parmigiana di Melanzane
dishes.desc: Baked layers of fried aubergine slices, tomato sauce, mozzarella or scamorza and Parmesan from southern Italy.

dishes.name: Orecchiette con Cime di Rapa
dishes.desc: Ear-shaped Apulian pasta tossed with bitter turnip greens, garlic, chilli, anchovies and olive oil.

dishes.name: Arancini
dishes.desc: Sicilian deep-fried rice balls stuffed with ragù, peas and cheese or ham and mozzarella, coated in breadcrumbs.

dishes.name: Pasta alla Norma
dishes.desc: Catanian pasta with tomato sauce, fried aubergine, basil and grated ricotta salata.

dishes.name: Caponata
dishes.desc: Sicilian sweet-and-sour stew of fried aubergine, celery, onions, capers, olives and tomato with vinegar and sugar.

dishes.name: Cannoli
dishes.desc: Sicilian crisp fried pastry tubes filled with sweetened sheep's ricotta, often with candied fruit or chocolate chips.

dishes.name: Cassata Siciliana
dishes.desc: Sicilian sponge cake layered with sweet ricotta, covered in marzipan and icing and decorated with candied fruit.

dishes.name: Granita
dishes.desc: Sicilian semi-frozen ice of sugar, water and lemon, almond, coffee or fruit, often eaten with brioche for breakfast.

dishes.name: Sfogliatella
dishes.desc: Neapolitan shell-shaped pastry of many crisp layers filled with semolina, ricotta and candied citrus.

dishes.name: Pasta con le Sarde
dishes.desc: Sicilian pasta with fresh sardines, wild fennel, raisins, pine nuts and saffron, topped with toasted breadcrumbs.

dishes.name: Pane Carasau
dishes.desc: Paper-thin, crisp Sardinian flatbread baked twice, traditionally made by shepherds to keep for months.

dishes.name: Malloreddus
dishes.desc: Small ridged Sardinian semolina gnocchi flavoured with saffron, typically served with sausage and tomato sauce.

dishes.name: Porceddu
dishes.desc: Sardinian suckling pig spit-roasted slowly over myrtle and juniper wood until the skin is crackling.

dishes.name: Burrata
dishes.desc: Fresh Apulian cheese of a mozzarella shell filled with creamy stracciatella, served with tomatoes and olive oil.

dishes.name: Mozzarella di Bufala
dishes.desc: Soft fresh cheese made from water buffalo milk in Campania, eaten fresh or in caprese salad.

dishes.name: Baba al Rum
dishes.desc: Small yeast-leavened cake soaked in rum syrup, a Neapolitan pastry-shop staple.

dishes.name: Limoncello
dishes.desc: Sweet, bright yellow lemon liqueur from the Amalfi Coast and Sorrento, served chilled after meals.

dishes.name: Gelato
dishes.desc: Italian ice cream denser and less airy than most, churned from milk, sugar and flavourings such as pistachio or hazelnut.

dishes.name: Espresso
dishes.desc: Small, strong coffee brewed by forcing hot water through finely ground beans under pressure, drunk standing at the bar.

dishes.name: Focaccia Barese
dishes.desc: Apulian focaccia with a potato-enriched dough, topped with cherry tomatoes, olives and oregano.

dishes.name: 'Nduja
dishes.desc: Spicy spreadable pork salami from Calabria, fiery with chilli, spread on bread or melted into sauces.

dishes.name: Insalata Caprese
dishes.desc: Capri salad of sliced tomatoes, mozzarella and basil dressed with olive oil.

dishes.name: Calzone
dishes.desc: Neapolitan pizza dough folded around ricotta, mozzarella and salami, baked or fried.

dishes.name: Panelle
dishes.desc: Palermo fritters of chickpea flour, eaten hot in a sesame bun.

dishes.name: Sfincione
dishes.desc: Thick spongy Palermo pizza topped with tomato, onions, anchovies, caciocavallo and breadcrumbs.

dishes.name: Taralli
dishes.desc: Crunchy ring-shaped Apulian biscuits made with olive oil and white wine, often with fennel seeds.

dishes.name: Croissant
dishes.desc: Crescent-shaped laminated pastry of buttery, flaky layers, eaten for breakfast with coffee.

dishes.name: Pain au Chocolat
dishes.desc: Rectangular laminated croissant dough rolled around sticks of dark chocolate.

dishes.name: Baguette
dishes.desc: Long, thin wheat loaf with a crisp crust and airy crumb, bought fresh daily from the boulangerie.

dishes.name: Steak Frites
dishes.desc: Pan-fried steak, often entrecôte or bavette, served with French fries and sometimes béarnaise or pepper sauce.

dishes.name: Croque Monsieur
dishes.desc: Toasted ham and cheese sandwich topped with béchamel and grated Gruyère, grilled until bubbling; a Parisian café staple.

dishes.name: Soupe à l'Oignon
dishes.desc: Soup of slowly caramelised onions in beef stock, topped with toasted bread and melted Gruyère.

dishes.name: Macarons
dishes.desc: Light almond-meringue sandwich cookies with ganache, buttercream or jam fillings in many colours.

dishes.name: Éclair
dishes.desc: Long choux pastry filled with custard cream and topped with chocolate or coffee icing.

dishes.name: Profiteroles
dishes.desc: Small choux pastry balls filled with cream or ice cream and covered with warm chocolate sauce.

dishes.name: Crêpes Suzette
dishes.desc: Thin crêpes in a sauce of caramelised sugar, butter, orange juice and zest, flambéed with Grand Marnier.

dishes.name: Brioche
dishes.desc: Rich, soft yeast bread made with plenty of eggs and butter, eaten for breakfast or as a sweet.

dishes.name: Crème Brûlée
dishes.desc: Rich vanilla custard topped with a layer of sugar caramelised into a hard glassy crust.

dishes.name: Blanquette de Veau
dishes.desc: Veal stewed in white stock with carrots and mushrooms, finished with a cream and egg-yolk sauce, served with rice.

dishes.name: Pot-au-feu
dishes.desc: Boiled beef with marrow bones, carrots, leeks and turnips, served as broth followed by meat and vegetables.

dishes.name: Steak Tartare
dishes.desc: Finely chopped raw beef mixed with capers, shallots, mustard and a raw egg yolk, served with fries.

dishes.name: Brie de Meaux
dishes.desc: Soft bloomy-rind cow's milk cheese from Meaux east of Paris, oozing and mushroomy when ripe.

dishes.name: Mille-Feuille
dishes.desc: Three layers of crisp puff pastry with vanilla pastry cream, topped with feathered icing.

dishes.name: Paris-Brest
dishes.desc: Wheel-shaped choux pastry filled with hazelnut praline cream, created for the Paris–Brest cycle race.

dishes.name: Ratatouille
dishes.desc: Provençal stewed vegetables: aubergine, courgette, peppers, onion and tomato cooked with olive oil and herbs.

dishes.name: Bouillabaisse
dishes.desc: Marseille fish stew of several Mediterranean rockfish and shellfish with saffron and fennel, served with rouille and croutons.

dishes.name: Salade Niçoise
dishes.desc: Nice salad of tomatoes, black olives, hard-boiled eggs, anchovies or tuna, green beans and olive oil.

dishes.name: Pissaladière
dishes.desc: Niçoise flatbread topped with slowly cooked onions, anchovies and black olives.

dishes.name: Tapenade
dishes.desc: Provençal spread of puréed black olives, capers, anchovies and olive oil, eaten on bread.

dishes.name: Socca
dishes.desc: Thin, crisp chickpea-flour pancake baked in a wood oven and sold hot with black pepper in Nice.

dishes.name: Aïoli
dishes.desc: Provençal garlic and olive oil emulsion, served as le grand aïoli with salt cod, boiled vegetables and eggs.

dishes.name: Daube Provençale
dishes.desc: Provençal beef stew braised slowly in red wine with garlic, herbs, orange peel and olives.

dishes.name: Tarte au Citron
dishes.desc: Shortcrust tart filled with tangy lemon curd, sometimes topped with meringue.

dishes.name: Calissons
dishes.desc: Diamond-shaped sweets from Aix-en-Provence made of candied melon and ground almonds under royal icing.

dishes.name: Pastis
dishes.desc: Anise-flavoured aperitif that turns milky with cold water, drunk on Provençal terraces.

dishes.name: Fougasse
dishes.desc: Leaf-shaped Provençal flatbread slashed into a pattern, flavoured with olives or herbs.

dishes.name: Brandade de Morue
dishes.desc: Nîmes purée of salt cod emulsified with olive oil, milk and garlic, served with toast.

dishes.name: Choucroute Garnie
dishes.desc: Alsatian sauerkraut braised in Riesling and served with sausages, smoked pork, bacon and potatoes.

dishes.name: Tarte Flambée
dishes.desc: Thin Alsatian flatbread spread with crème fraîche and topped with onions and lardons, baked in a hot oven.

dishes.name: Quiche Lorraine
dishes.desc: Open pastry tart filled with a custard of eggs and cream with smoked bacon lardons.

dishes.name: Baeckeoffe
dishes.desc: Alsatian casserole of marinated pork, lamb and beef layered with potatoes and onions in white wine, sealed with dough.

dishes.name: Kouglof
dishes.desc: Alsatian ring-shaped yeast cake with raisins and almonds, baked in a fluted mould and dusted with sugar.

dishes.name: Fondue Savoyarde
dishes.desc: Alpine dish of Comté, Beaufort and Emmental melted with white wine, eaten by dipping bread cubes.

dishes.name: Raclette
dishes.desc: Alpine dish of raclette cheese melted and scraped over boiled potatoes, served with cured meats and pickles.

dishes.name: Tartiflette
dishes.desc: Savoyard gratin of potatoes, lardons, onions and a whole Reblochon cheese baked until melting.

dishes.name: Gratin Dauphinois
dishes.desc: Thinly sliced potatoes baked slowly in cream and milk with garlic, from the Dauphiné.

dishes.name: Madeleines
dishes.desc: Small shell-shaped butter sponge cakes from Commercy in Lorraine.

dishes.name: Comté
dishes.desc: Nutty hard cheese from the Jura mountains, made in village dairies from raw cow's milk and aged for months.

dishes.name: Champagne
dishes.desc: Sparkling wine from the Champagne region, made with a second fermentation in the bottle.

dishes.name: Munster
dishes.desc: Pungent washed-rind cow's milk cheese from the Vosges, eaten with cumin and boiled potatoes.

dishes.name: Boeuf Bourguignon
dishes.desc: Burgundian beef stew braised in red wine with lardons, mushrooms, pearl onions and herbs.

dishes.name: Coq au Vin
dishes.desc: Chicken braised in red wine with lardons, mushrooms and onions, a Burgundian classic.

dishes.name: Quenelles de Brochet
dishes.desc: Lyonnaise poached dumplings of pike mousse bound with panade, baked in creamy Nantua crayfish sauce.

dishes.name: Andouillette
dishes.desc: Coarse, strong-smelling sausage of pork chitterlings and tripe, grilled and served with mustard, notably in Lyon and Troyes.

dishes.name: Gougères
dishes.desc: Savoury Burgundian choux pastry puffs baked with Gruyère or Comté, served with wine as an aperitif.

dishes.name: Escargots de Bourgogne
dishes.desc: Burgundy snails baked in their shells with garlic-parsley butter and served sizzling with bread.

dishes.name: Jambon Persillé
dishes.desc: Burgundian terrine of chunks of ham set in parsley-flecked white-wine aspic, traditionally eaten at Easter.

dishes.name: Rillettes
dishes.desc: Pork slowly cooked in its own fat, shredded and potted, spread on bread; speciality of Tours and Le Mans.

dishes.name: Galette des Rois
dishes.desc: Puff pastry cake filled with frangipane, containing a hidden charm, eaten at Epiphany in January.

dishes.name: Tarte Tatin
dishes.desc: Upside-down tart of apples caramelised in butter and sugar, baked under pastry and inverted to serve.

dishes.name: Saucisson Sec
dishes.desc: Dry-cured pork sausage, such as the Rosette de Lyon, sliced thick and eaten with bread and wine.

dishes.name: Salade Lyonnaise
dishes.desc: Frisée salad with crisp lardons, croutons and a poached egg in mustard vinaigrette, a Lyon bouchon classic.

dishes.name: Cassoulet
dishes.desc: Slow-cooked casserole of white beans with duck confit, Toulouse sausage and pork from Languedoc.

dishes.name: Confit de Canard
dishes.desc: Duck legs salted and slowly cooked in their own fat, then crisped and served with potatoes from Gascony.

dishes.name: Foie Gras
dishes.desc: Rich, buttery liver of specially fattened duck or goose, served as a terrine or pan-seared, especially at Christmas.

dishes.name: Magret de Canard
dishes.desc: Breast of fattened Moulard duck, seared skin-side down and served pink, a speciality of the southwest.

dishes.name: Galette Bretonne
dishes.desc: Breton savoury buckwheat crêpe, classically filled with ham, egg and Emmental and folded square.

dishes.name: Crêpe au Beurre Salé
dishes.desc: Thin Breton wheat crêpe simply spread with salted butter and sugar or salted-butter caramel.

dishes.name: Kouign-amann
dishes.desc: Breton cake of laminated bread dough folded with butter and sugar and baked until caramelised.

dishes.name: Moules Marinières
dishes.desc: Mussels steamed with white wine, shallots, butter and parsley, often served with fries.

dishes.name: Canelé
dishes.desc: Small Bordeaux pastry flavoured with rum and vanilla, with a dark caramelised crust and custardy centre.

dishes.name: Piperade
dishes.desc: Basque sauté of onions, green peppers and tomatoes seasoned with Espelette pepper, often with eggs or ham.

dishes.name: Roquefort
dishes.desc: Pungent blue sheep's milk cheese ripened in the natural caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

dishes.name: Jambon de Bayonne
dishes.desc: Dry-cured ham from the Adour basin, rubbed with salt from Salies-de-Béarn and sometimes Espelette pepper.

dishes.name: Camembert
dishes.desc: Soft bloomy-rind cow's milk cheese from Normandy, sold in round wooden boxes.

dishes.name: Gâteau Basque
dishes.desc: Buttery Basque cake filled with pastry cream or black cherry jam.

dishes.name: Aligot
dishes.desc: Mashed potato beaten with garlic and Tomme cheese until it stretches in ribbons, from the Aubrac plateau.

dishes.name: Tortilla Española
dishes.desc: Thick omelette of eggs, potatoes slowly fried in olive oil and usually onion, served in wedges as tapa.

dishes.name: Patatas Bravas
dishes.desc: Fried potato cubes served with spicy tomato-paprika bravas sauce and often aioli, a tapas bar classic.

dishes.name: Jamón Ibérico
dishes.desc: Dry-cured ham from black Iberian pigs, often acorn-fed, aged for years and sliced thinly by hand.

dishes.name: Croquetas
dishes.desc: Fried breaded croquettes of thick béchamel with jamón, chicken or salt cod, served as tapas.

dishes.name: Churros con Chocolate
dishes.desc: Fried ridged dough sticks dusted with sugar and dipped into thick hot chocolate, often for breakfast.

dishes.name: Pimientos de Padrón
dishes.desc: Small green Galician peppers blistered in olive oil and sprinkled with sea salt; occasional ones are hot.

dishes.name: Gambas al Ajillo
dishes.desc: Prawns sizzled in olive oil with plenty of garlic and dried chilli, served in an earthenware dish.

dishes.name: Albóndigas
dishes.desc: Pork and beef meatballs simmered in tomato or almond sauce, served as tapa.

dishes.name: Pan con Tomate
dishes.desc: Toasted bread rubbed with ripe tomato and garlic, drizzled with olive oil and salt, of Catalan origin.

dishes.name: Manchego
dishes.desc: Firm sheep's milk cheese from La Mancha with a zigzag rind, served in wedges with membrillo.

dishes.name: Turrón
dishes.desc: Nougat of honey, sugar, egg white and almonds, hard from Alicante or soft from Jijona, eaten at Christmas.

dishes.name: Sangria
dishes.desc: Punch of red wine, chopped fruit, sugar and often brandy or orange liqueur, served chilled.

dishes.name: Ensaladilla Rusa
dishes.desc: Potato salad with tuna, carrots, peas, egg and mayonnaise, served as a tapa in nearly every bar.

dishes.name: Salpicón de Marisco
dishes.desc: Chilled seafood salad of prawns, octopus and mussels with diced peppers and onion in vinaigrette.

dishes.name: Tinto de Verano
dishes.desc: Red wine mixed with lemon soda over ice, the everyday Spanish summer drink.

dishes.name: Chorizo
dishes.desc: Cured pork sausage coloured and flavoured with smoked paprika and garlic, sliced as tapa or cooked into stews.

dishes.name: Gazpacho
dishes.desc: Andalusian cold soup of blended raw tomatoes, cucumber, peppers, garlic, olive oil and vinegar.

dishes.name: Salmorejo
dishes.desc: Thick cold Córdoban purée of tomatoes, bread, garlic and olive oil, topped with jamón and boiled egg.

dishes.name: Pescaíto Frito
dishes.desc: Assorted small fish and squid dusted in flour and deep-fried in olive oil, an Andalusian coastal favourite.

dishes.name: Rabo de Toro
dishes.desc: Córdoban oxtail stew braised in red wine with vegetables until the meat falls off the bone.

dishes.name: Espetos de Sardinas
dishes.desc: Sardines skewered on canes and grilled over wood fires on the beaches of Málaga.

dishes.name: Flamenquín
dishes.desc: Córdoban roll of pork loin wrapped around jamón, breaded and deep-fried.

dishes.name: Berenjenas con Miel
dishes.desc: Fried aubergine strips drizzled with sugarcane molasses or honey, a tapa from Córdoba and Málaga.

dishes.name: Boquerones en Vinagre
dishes.desc: Fresh anchovy fillets cured in vinegar and dressed with garlic, parsley and olive oil, a tapa classic.

dishes.name: Sherry
dishes.desc: Fortified wine from Jerez de la Frontera, from bone-dry fino to sweet Pedro Ximénez.

dishes.name: Polvorones
dishes.desc: Crumbly Christmas shortbread of toasted flour, lard, sugar and almonds, wrapped in paper.

dishes.name: Paella Valenciana
dishes.desc: Valencian rice cooked in a wide pan with chicken, rabbit, green and butter beans, saffron and rosemary.

dishes.name: Paella de Marisco
dishes.desc: Saffron rice cooked in a wide pan with prawns, mussels, squid and clams in seafood stock.

dishes.name: Fideuà
dishes.desc: Valencian dish like paella but made with short thin noodles, cooked with seafood in fish stock and served with aioli.

dishes.name: Arroz Negro
dishes.desc: Valencian and Catalan rice cooked with squid or cuttlefish and their ink, served with aioli.

dishes.name: Calçots con Romesco
dishes.desc: Catalan sweet green onions charred over flames and dipped in nutty romesco sauce, eaten at winter calçotadas.

dishes.name: Escalivada
dishes.desc: Catalan dish of smoky fire-roasted aubergines, peppers and onions dressed with olive oil.

dishes.name: Horchata
dishes.desc: Chilled sweet milky drink made from soaked, ground tiger nuts, a Valencian summer speciality.

dishes.name: Suquet de Peix
dishes.desc: Catalan fisherman's stew of fish and potatoes in a broth thickened with picada of almonds and garlic.

dishes.name: Crema Catalana
dishes.desc: Catalan custard flavoured with lemon zest and cinnamon, topped with a crisp layer of caramelised sugar.

dishes.name: Cava
dishes.desc: Catalan sparkling wine made in the traditional method, mostly around Sant Sadurní d'Anoia.

dishes.name: Botifarra amb Mongetes
dishes.desc: Grilled Catalan pork sausage with white beans fried in pork fat.

dishes.name: Pintxos
dishes.desc: Basque bar snacks, often a small slice of bread topped with seafood, ham or tortilla and held with a skewer.

dishes.name: Bacalao al Pil-Pil
dishes.desc: Basque salt cod cooked gently in olive oil with garlic and chilli until its gelatine emulsifies into a sauce.

dishes.name: Txuleta
dishes.desc: Basque thick-cut bone-in rib steak from older cattle, grilled over coals and served rare with coarse salt.

dishes.name: Marmitako
dishes.desc: Basque fishermen's stew of tuna, potatoes, peppers, onions and tomatoes.

dishes.name: Fabada Asturiana
dishes.desc: Asturian stew of large white fabes beans with chorizo, morcilla blood sausage and pork belly.

dishes.name: Pulpo a la Gallega
dishes.desc: Galician boiled octopus sliced on wooden plates with olive oil, sea salt and paprika, often over potatoes.

dishes.name: Tarta de Santiago
dishes.desc: Galician almond cake with a powdered-sugar cross of St James, associated with Santiago de Compostela.

dishes.name: Tarta de Queso Vasca
dishes.desc: Crustless cheesecake baked at high heat until deeply burnt on top and creamy inside, from San Sebastián.

dishes.name: Empanada Gallega
dishes.desc: Large Galician pie of bread-like dough filled with tuna, onions and peppers or other fillings, sliced to serve.

dishes.name: Cachopo
dishes.desc: Asturian dish of two large breaded veal fillets sandwiching ham and cheese, deep-fried.

dishes.name: Leche Frita
dishes.desc: Firm milk custard cut into squares, breaded and fried, then dusted with cinnamon sugar.

dishes.name: Idiazabal
dishes.desc: Lightly smoked hard cheese of raw latxa sheep's milk from the Basque Country and Navarre.

dishes.name: Cabrales
dishes.desc: Strong blue cheese from Asturias, ripened in limestone caves of the Picos de Europa.

dishes.name: Sidra Asturiana
dishes.desc: Natural Asturian cider poured from high above the head to aerate it, drunk in one gulp.

dishes.name: Cocido Madrileño
dishes.desc: Madrid chickpea stew with meats, chorizo and vegetables, served in courses: broth with noodles, then chickpeas and meat.

dishes.name: Bocadillo de Calamares
dishes.desc: Madrid sandwich of fried battered squid rings in a crusty baguette, sold around Plaza Mayor.

dishes.name: Cochinillo Asado
dishes.desc: Segovian suckling pig roasted until the skin is crisp enough to cut with a plate's edge.

dishes.name: Huevos Rotos
dishes.desc: Fried eggs broken over fried potatoes, usually with jamón or chorizo.

dishes.name: Migas
dishes.desc: Shepherd's dish of breadcrumbs fried in olive oil with garlic, chorizo and peppers.

dishes.name: Callos a la Madrileña
dishes.desc: Madrid stew of beef tripe with chorizo, morcilla and paprika.

dishes.name: Torrijas
dishes.desc: Slices of bread soaked in milk or wine, dipped in egg, fried and sweetened with honey or cinnamon sugar, eaten at Easter.

dishes.name: Pisto
dishes.desc: Manchego stew of slowly cooked tomatoes, peppers, onions and courgette, often topped with a fried egg.

dishes.name: Lechazo Asado
dishes.desc: Milk-fed lamb roasted in a wood oven with only water and salt, the pride of Castilla y León.

dishes.name: Sopa de Ajo
dishes.desc: Castilian garlic soup with paprika, stale bread and a poached egg, often with a little jamón.

dishes.name: Papas Arrugadas con Mojo
dishes.desc: Small Canarian potatoes boiled in very salty water until wrinkled, served with red and green mojo sauces.

dishes.name: Gofio
dishes.desc: Toasted grain flour of the Canary Islands, stirred into milk and soups or kneaded into a dough.

dishes.name: Sancocho Canario
dishes.desc: Canarian stew of salted fish with potatoes and sweet potato, served with mojo and gofio.

dishes.name: Ensaimada
dishes.desc: Mallorcan spiral pastry of sweet dough made with pork lard, dusted with powdered sugar.

dishes.name: Sobrasada
dishes.desc: Soft, spreadable Mallorcan pork sausage seasoned with paprika, spread on bread or drizzled with honey.

dishes.name: Tumbet
dishes.desc: Mallorcan layered bake of fried potatoes, aubergine and red peppers under tomato sauce.

dishes.name: Caldereta de Langosta
dishes.desc: Menorcan spiny lobster stew with tomato, onion and garlic, served over thin slices of bread.

dishes.name: Queso Mahón
dishes.desc: Square cow's milk cheese from Menorca with an orange rind rubbed with oil and paprika.

dishes.name: Pastel de Nata
dishes.desc: Custard tart of crisp puff pastry with a caramelised egg custard filling, dusted with cinnamon; famous from Belém.

dishes.name: Bacalhau à Brás
dishes.desc: Shredded salt cod scrambled with matchstick fried potatoes, onions and eggs, garnished with olives and parsley.

dishes.name: Bacalhau com Natas
dishes.desc: Baked casserole of salt cod, potatoes and onions in cream and béchamel sauce.

dishes.name: Francesinha
dishes.desc: Porto sandwich of layered meats and sausage covered with melted cheese and a hot beer-tomato sauce, served with fries.

dishes.name: Caldo Verde
dishes.desc: Soup of puréed potatoes with finely shredded kale, olive oil and slices of chouriço, from the Minho.

dishes.name: Sardinhas Assadas
dishes.desc: Fresh sardines grilled over charcoal and served on bread, essential at Lisbon's June Santo António festivals.

dishes.name: Arroz de Marisco
dishes.desc: Soupy rice cooked with prawns, clams, mussels and crab in a tomato and seafood broth.

dishes.name: Cataplana
dishes.desc: Algarve seafood or pork-and-clam stew cooked in a hinged copper clam-shaped pan of the same name.

dishes.name: Bifana
dishes.desc: Lisbon sandwich of thin pork slices marinated in garlic and wine, served in a soft roll with mustard.

dishes.name: Leitão Assado
dishes.desc: Bairrada-style suckling pig spit-roasted with a garlic-pepper paste until the skin is crackling.

dishes.name: Polvo à Lagareiro
dishes.desc: Octopus boiled then roasted with plenty of olive oil, garlic and small punched potatoes.

dishes.name: Pastéis de Bacalhau
dishes.desc: Fried oval croquettes of salt cod, potato, egg and parsley, eaten as snacks or starters.

dishes.name: Alheira
dishes.desc: Smoked sausage from Trás-os-Montes of poultry or game and bread, created by Jews to appear pork-eating.

dishes.name: Feijoada à Transmontana
dishes.desc: Northern Portuguese stew of red or white beans with pork, smoked sausages and cabbage.

dishes.name: Queijo da Serra
dishes.desc: Soft, runny sheep's milk cheese from Serra da Estrela, curdled with thistle and eaten with a spoon.

dishes.name: Ovos Moles
dishes.desc: Sweet from Aveiro of egg yolks and sugar enclosed in thin wafer shells shaped like seashells.

dishes.name: Arroz Doce
dishes.desc: Creamy rice pudding cooked with milk, lemon zest and egg yolks, decorated with cinnamon patterns.

dishes.name: Bola de Berlim
dishes.desc: Doughnut filled with egg-yolk custard, sold on beaches in summer.

dishes.name: Ginjinha
dishes.desc: Lisbon sour-cherry liqueur made from ginja berries in aguardente, served in small shots.

dishes.name: Porco à Alentejana
dishes.desc: Alentejo dish of marinated fried pork cubes combined with clams, potatoes and coriander.

dishes.name: Frango Piri-Piri
dishes.desc: Grilled chicken basted with hot piri-piri chilli, garlic and olive oil, a speciality of the Algarve.

dishes.name: Port Wine
dishes.desc: Sweet fortified wine from the Douro Valley, aged in Porto's cellars and drunk as dessert wine.

dishes.name: Prego
dishes.desc: Sandwich of a thin garlic-marinated beef steak in a crusty roll, often with mustard.

dishes.name: Pão com Chouriço
dishes.desc: Bread baked with slices of chouriço sausage inside, a staple at Portuguese festivals and pilgrimages.

dishes.name: Cozido à Portuguesa
dishes.desc: Boiled feast of beef, pork, chicken, chouriço and blood sausage with cabbage, potatoes and carrots.

dishes.name: Amêijoas à Bulhão Pato
dishes.desc: Clams steamed with olive oil, garlic, coriander and lemon, named after a 19th-century poet.

dishes.name: Presunto
dishes.desc: Dry-cured Portuguese ham, such as presunto de Chaves or from black Alentejo pigs, sliced thin.

dishes.name: Pão de Ló
dishes.desc: Airy sponge cake of eggs, sugar and flour, in some towns baked runny in the centre.

dishes.name: Açorda
dishes.desc: Alentejo soup of bread soaked in garlic and coriander broth with olive oil and a poached egg.

dishes.name: Bolo do Caco
dishes.desc: Madeiran sweet-potato flatbread cooked on a basalt stone and spread with garlic butter.

dishes.name: Espetada Madeirense
dishes.desc: Madeiran beef chunks rubbed with garlic and salt, grilled on bay-laurel skewers.

dishes.name: Moussaka
dishes.desc: Baked layers of aubergine, spiced minced lamb or beef in tomato sauce and a thick béchamel topping.

dishes.name: Souvlaki
dishes.desc: Grilled skewers of pork or chicken, eaten on the stick or in pita with tzatziki, onions and tomato.

dishes.name: Gyros
dishes.desc: Meat roasted on a vertical rotisserie, shaved and wrapped in pita with tzatziki, tomato, onion and fries.

dishes.name: Greek Salad
dishes.desc: Salad of tomatoes, cucumber, onion, green pepper, olives and a slab of feta with oregano and olive oil.

dishes.name: Tzatziki
dishes.desc: Dip of strained yoghurt with grated cucumber, garlic, olive oil and dill or mint.

dishes.name: Spanakopita
dishes.desc: Pie of flaky filo pastry filled with spinach, feta, onions and herbs.

dishes.name: Tiropita
dishes.desc: Filo pastry pie filled with a mixture of feta cheese and eggs, a common bakery snack.

dishes.name: Dolmades
dishes.desc: Vine leaves rolled around rice with herbs, sometimes minced meat, served with lemon or avgolemono.

dishes.name: Pastitsio
dishes.desc: Baked layers of tubular pasta, spiced meat sauce and thick béchamel, Greece's answer to lasagne.

dishes.name: Gemista
dishes.desc: Tomatoes and peppers stuffed with herbed rice, sometimes minced meat, and baked with olive oil and potatoes.

dishes.name: Kleftiko
dishes.desc: Lamb slow-roasted with garlic, lemon and herbs, sealed in parchment or clay so it cooks in its juices.

dishes.name: Stifado
dishes.desc: Stew of beef or rabbit with many small onions in red wine, tomato and cinnamon.

dishes.name: Fava Santorinis
dishes.desc: Smooth purée of yellow split peas from Santorini, topped with olive oil, onions and capers.

dishes.name: Saganaki
dishes.desc: Firm cheese such as kefalograviera pan-fried until crusty and served with lemon.

dishes.name: Keftedes
dishes.desc: Fried meatballs of minced meat with onion, mint and oregano, served as meze.

dishes.name: Loukoumades
dishes.desc: Small fried dough balls soaked in honey syrup and sprinkled with cinnamon and walnuts.

dishes.name: Baklava
dishes.desc: Layers of filo pastry filled with chopped walnuts and almonds, soaked in honey syrup.

dishes.name: Galaktoboureko
dishes.desc: Filo pastry filled with semolina custard and soaked in lemon-scented syrup.

dishes.name: Bougatsa
dishes.desc: Thessaloniki breakfast pastry of filo filled with semolina custard, cheese or minced meat, dusted with sugar and cinnamon.

dishes.name: Grilled Octopus
dishes.desc: Sun-dried octopus tentacles grilled over charcoal and dressed with olive oil, vinegar and oregano, served with ouzo.

dishes.name: Avgolemono Soup
dishes.desc: Chicken broth with rice or orzo thickened with a whisked egg and lemon mixture.

dishes.name: Taramasalata
dishes.desc: Dip of salted fish roe whipped with bread or potato, olive oil and lemon juice.

dishes.name: Koulouri
dishes.desc: Ring-shaped bread covered with sesame seeds, sold by street vendors in Thessaloniki and Athens.

dishes.name: Fasolada
dishes.desc: White bean soup with tomatoes, carrots, celery and plenty of olive oil, often called Greece's national dish.

dishes.name: Ouzo
dishes.desc: Anise-flavoured spirit drunk with water and ice, turning milky white, alongside meze.

dishes.name: Frappé
dishes.desc: Iced coffee of instant coffee shaken with water, sugar and ice into a thick foam.

dishes.name: Feta
dishes.desc: Brined white cheese of sheep's and goat's milk, crumbled over salads or baked with tomatoes and oregano.

dishes.name: Gigantes Plaki
dishes.desc: Giant white beans baked in tomato sauce with dill, onion and plenty of olive oil.

dishes.name: Retsina
dishes.desc: White wine flavoured with Aleppo pine resin, drunk cold with meze.

dishes.name: Greek Coffee
dishes.desc: Finely ground coffee boiled in a small briki and served unfiltered under its foam.

dishes.name: Melitzanosalata
dishes.desc: Smoky dip of charred aubergine mashed with garlic, olive oil, lemon and parsley.

dishes.name: Weißwurst
dishes.desc: Bavarian white sausage of minced veal and pork back bacon, boiled and eaten before noon with sweet mustard and pretzels.

dishes.name: Schweinshaxe
dishes.desc: Bavarian roasted pork knuckle with crackling skin, served with dumplings, sauerkraut and beer.

dishes.name: Schnitzel
dishes.desc: Thin pork or veal escalope coated in breadcrumbs and pan-fried, served with lemon, potatoes or fries.

dishes.name: Obatzda
dishes.desc: Bavarian beer-garden spread of ripe Camembert, butter, onions, paprika and beer, eaten with pretzels.

dishes.name: Brezel
dishes.desc: Lye-dipped knotted bread with a shiny brown crust and coarse salt, especially from Bavaria and Swabia.

dishes.name: Käsespätzle
dishes.desc: Swabian and Allgäu egg noodles layered with grated cheese and topped with crispy fried onions.

dishes.name: Leberkäse
dishes.desc: Bavarian baked loaf of finely ground pork and beef, sliced thick and served warm in a roll with mustard.

dishes.name: Maultaschen
dishes.desc: Swabian large pasta pockets filled with minced meat, spinach, bread and onions, served in broth or fried.

dishes.name: Semmelknödel
dishes.desc: Bavarian dumplings of stale bread rolls, milk, eggs and parsley, served with roasts and gravy.

dishes.name: Spätzle
dishes.desc: Swabian soft egg noodles made by scraping or pressing batter into boiling water, served with roasts.

dishes.name: Black Forest Cake
dishes.desc: Layers of chocolate sponge, kirsch-soaked cherries and whipped cream, decorated with chocolate shavings.

dishes.name: Lebkuchen
dishes.desc: Spiced honey gingerbread with nuts and candied peel, especially from Nuremberg, eaten at Christmas markets.

dishes.name: Weißbier
dishes.desc: Top-fermented Bavarian wheat beer, cloudy and with banana and clove notes, served in tall glasses.

dishes.name: Black Forest Ham
dishes.desc: Schwarzwälder Schinken: boneless ham cured with juniper and garlic, then cold-smoked over fir wood.

dishes.name: Nürnberger Rostbratwurst
dishes.desc: Finger-sized marjoram pork sausages grilled over beech wood, served by the six or three in a roll.

dishes.name: Bienenstich
dishes.desc: Yeast cake filled with vanilla cream and topped with caramelised honey and almonds.

dishes.name: Labskaus
dishes.desc: Northern German sailor's mash of corned beef, potatoes and beetroot, served with fried egg, pickled gherkin and rollmops.

dishes.name: Fischbrötchen
dishes.desc: Bread roll filled with pickled herring or other fish, onions and remoulade, sold at harbour stands on the North Sea coast.

dishes.name: Currywurst
dishes.desc: Sliced fried pork sausage smothered in curry-spiced ketchup, served with fries; a Berlin street food icon.

dishes.name: Königsberger Klopse
dishes.desc: Poached meatballs in a white sauce with capers and lemon, served with boiled potatoes.

dishes.name: Rouladen
dishes.desc: Thin beef slices rolled around bacon, onions and pickles, braised and served with red cabbage and dumplings.

dishes.name: Hamburger Aalsuppe
dishes.desc: Hamburg sweet-and-sour soup with dried fruit, vegetables, ham and sometimes eel, flavoured with herbs.

dishes.name: Grünkohl mit Pinkel
dishes.desc: Northern German winter dish of stewed kale with smoked Pinkel grain sausage, pork and boiled potatoes.

dishes.name: Berliner Pfannkuchen
dishes.desc: Fried yeast doughnut without a hole, filled with jam and dusted with sugar, eaten especially at New Year and Carnival.

dishes.name: Eisbein
dishes.desc: Pickled ham hock simmered until tender, served with sauerkraut and pease pudding, typical of Berlin.

dishes.name: Rote Grütze
dishes.desc: Northern German pudding of red berries cooked with juice and thickened, served with vanilla sauce or cream.

dishes.name: Bratkartoffeln
dishes.desc: Sliced boiled potatoes pan-fried with onions and bacon until golden.

dishes.name: Stollen
dishes.desc: Dense Christmas fruit bread with dried fruit, candied peel, marzipan and a thick coat of icing sugar, famous from Dresden.

dishes.name: Döner Kebab
dishes.desc: Berlin-style sandwich of meat shaved from a rotisserie stuffed into toasted flatbread with salad and sauces.

dishes.name: Bratwurst
dishes.desc: Grilled or fried pork sausage, served with mustard in a bread roll or with sauerkraut and potatoes.

dishes.name: Kartoffelsalat
dishes.desc: Potato salad, dressed with broth and vinegar in the south or with mayonnaise in the north.

dishes.name: Sauerkraut
dishes.desc: Finely cut white cabbage fermented with salt, cooked as a side dish with pork and sausages.

dishes.name: Flammkuchen
dishes.desc: Thin flatbread spread with crème fraîche and topped with onions and bacon, from the Palatinate and Baden.

dishes.name: Himmel un Ääd
dishes.desc: Rhineland dish of mashed potatoes and apple sauce served with fried black pudding and onions.

dishes.name: Reibekuchen
dishes.desc: Fried pancakes of grated potato and onion, served with apple sauce, typical of the Rhineland.

dishes.name: Pumpernickel
dishes.desc: Dense, dark Westphalian rye bread baked slowly at low temperature for many hours, giving it a sweet flavour.

dishes.name: Frankfurter Grüne Soße
dishes.desc: Frankfurt cold sauce of seven fresh herbs with sour cream and yoghurt, served with boiled eggs and potatoes.

dishes.name: Eintopf
dishes.desc: One-pot thick stew of pulses or vegetables with potatoes and sausage or meat, everyday German home cooking.

dishes.name: Spargel mit Sauce Hollandaise
dishes.desc: Seasonal white asparagus boiled and served with hollandaise sauce, new potatoes and ham during spring asparagus season.

dishes.name: Streuselkuchen
dishes.desc: Yeast sheet cake topped with crumbly butter-sugar streusel, often over fruit, popular from Silesia.

dishes.name: Glühwein
dishes.desc: Hot red wine spiced with cinnamon, cloves and orange, sold at Christmas markets.

dishes.name: Sauerbraten
dishes.desc: Pot roast of beef marinated for days in vinegar, wine and spices, served with a sweet-sour gravy.

dishes.name: Kölsch
dishes.desc: Pale, crisp top-fermented beer of Cologne, served in small straight glasses that keep being refilled.

dishes.name: Apfelschorle
dishes.desc: Apple juice mixed with sparkling mineral water, Germany's everyday soft drink.
